messages:
anika: Heads-up — after rolling kernel-routing v2.3 to prod last night, we see a sustained drop in KV prefetch/prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of small-sequence workloads. Was ~82% -> ~48% on the affected tenants. Noticed around 01:20UTC. :eyes:

raj: Ugh. Any single-change suspects? kernel routing + new attention tiling + quant profile switch landed together in the rollout.

maria: Perf-bot posted a summary in #alerts, attaching the quick numbers: perf-bot: before=0.822 avg_hit, after=0.481 avg_hit, drop_group=chat-sdk-small, p95-latency +18%.

anika: Relevant excerpt from trace (simplified):
```
[trace] request_id=rc_99a1 prefix_hash_incoming=0x7f2a build_id=build-2026-03-05 kernel_variant=tiling-v2 quant_profile=q8_2
[cache] computed_key = H(prefix || model_id || quant_profile || padding_info)
[cache] miss -> backend infer + cache_write
```

tim: Wait — I thought we intentionally avoided padding_info in the canonical key. Did that change?

raj: It looks like the kernel's new tiling introduced deterministic trailing zeros in intermediate token buffers for small sequences. A small change in the compile pipeline started attaching a padding descriptor to the runtime metadata. That metadata is now being passed into the cache key routine via the new kernel ABI.

maria: Snippet from kernel handshake log: `KERNEL_TAG: tiling-v2|pad_align=32|tile=64`. Prior builds didn't expose pad_align. The cache key code path serializes whatever metadata is present, so pad_align ended up in keys.

anika: So different pad_align values between hosts (32 vs 64) => same prefix but different key => miss. That explains tenant-specific effect (some Dedicated hosts got variant A, others B). :facepalm:

perf-bot: quick histogram from canary traces attached:
- host-group-a (pad_align=32): hit=0.79
- host-group-b (pad_align=64): hit=0.47
- cross-host requests show low interop reusage

raj: Short-term mitigation: force key canonicalization in the runtime to ignore pad_align and other non-semantic kernel metadata. I can ship a small patch to the cache key computation to filter out known-noise tags.

tim: Can we hotfix? deploy-bot: we can do a rolling config patch to disable passing kernel metadata into cache-key serialization in prod. But need a quick test on canary first.

maria: Also observed that batching heuristics changed grouping boundaries, so continuous-batcher is combining a few tiny requests into a single batch differently, which slightly alters prefix order in some code paths. Might be a second-order effect but worth checking.

sre-oncall: Impact: several customers reported latency spikes and error budgets creeping. We're throttling non-critical workloads on affected nodes while team triages.

anika: Proposed short-term plan:
- raj: prepare key-canonicalization patch (ignore pad_align, tile param) -> canary deploy to 10 hosts (owner: raj)
- tim: run end-to-end warmup harness against canary with representative chat-sdk-small workload (owner: tim)
- maria: compare batch group histograms pre/post to confirm batching impact (owner: maria)
- if canary restores hit-rate -> roll to prod with 1h ramp; otherwise rollback kernel routing v2.3 (owner: everyoneteam)

raj: Draft patch (inline):
```
- serialize(kernel_meta) into cache_key
+ filtered = filter(kernel_meta, allowed_keys=['model_id','quant_profile','build_id'])
+ serialize(filtered) into cache_key
```
I'll open PR in a few minutes.

maria: Also adding a safety: add a checksum field for normalized-prefix to detect accidental differences (not used in lookup, just for telemetry) so we can root-cause future drift.

tim: Test cases to add to CI: varying pad_align values produce identical cache_key after canonicalization, and inter-host lookup tests that exercise dedup.

anika: Good. If we can get numbers from canary within 30m we can decide. Anyone can flag if we need to escalate to rolling rollback.

perf-bot: Canary run #12: hit-rate on canary hosts improved from 0.49 -> 0.81 after applying raj's patch. p95 latency dropped -14%.

maria: Verified batching histogram shows same group boundaries after patch. Looks like key canonicalization fixed the majority; batching change was a red herring.

tim: Timed actions: canary->gradual-prod at +30m, full roll complete by +3h if stable.

sre-oncall: Noted. I'll keep throttles in place until prod roll finishes. Logging will include extra telemetry: normalized_prefix_checksum, kernel_variant_reported.

anika: Follow-ups:
- retrospective writeup (owner: anika) documenting kernel ABI contracts and cache-key rules
- add integration test in runtime CI to assert kernel metadata doesn't leak into keys (owner: raj)
- consider making kernel-to-runtime metadata explicit (schema) rather than freeform (owner: maria)

raj: Opening PR now: https://git.internal/repo/pull/3489 :rocket:

maria: Nice quick win. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

anika: Closing loop once prod stable. If anyone sees new anomalies ping me or @sre-oncall.

deploy-bot: Rolling config patch applied to canary hosts at 2412345820.

perf-bot: Prod roll started at 2412345900 (gradual). Monitoring for 60m.

sre-oncall: Prod roll +30m check-in: hit-rate back to baseline across all hosts. Removing throttles.

anika: Great job team. Will capture action items in the retro doc.
